newsitem.title: THAILAND: Banpu group in Thai power pact.
newsitem.headline: Banpu group in Thai power pact.

text.p: State-run Electricity Generating Authority of Thailand (EGAT) said on Thursday it signed a power purchase agreement with a group led by Bangkok-based Banpu Plc under the first-stage Independent Power Producer scheme.

The group, known as Tri Energy, comprised Banpu Plc which holds a 50 percent stake, Texaco Inc with 40 percent and private firm Black & Veatch Power Development Corp of the U.S. with 10 percent, EGAT said in a statement.
Under the agreement, EGAT will buy power from the group's 700-megawatt combined-cycle power plant in Ratchaburi, west of Bangkok, for 20 years starting May 2000, it said.
The agency plans to buy 4,200 megawatts of power from independent producers by 2002 to meet Thailand's growing demand.
